content: 26. Sort an array of objects in JavaScript

To sort an array of objects in JavaScript, you can pass a compare function as an argument to the `sort` method. Here's an example:

```javascript
const movies = [
  { title: 'The Shawshank Redemption', year: 1994 },
  { title: 'The Godfather', year: 1972 },
  { title: 'The Dark Knight', year: 2008 },
  { title: '12 Angry Men', year: 1957 },
];

movies.sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year);
```

In this example, the `sort` method takes a compare function that compares the `year` property of each object. The function subtracts the `year` of `a` from the `year` of `b`, which will result in a negative number if `a`'s year is earlier than `b`'s year, a positive number if `a`'s year is later than `b`'s year, or zero if they have the same year. 

The `sort` method then uses this compare function to sort the `movies` array in ascending order by year.

Yes, certainly! Here's an example of how to sort an array of objects in descending order based on a property value:

```javascript
const movies = [
  { title: 'The Shawshank Redemption', year: 1994 },
  { title: 'The Godfather', year: 1972 },
  { title: 'The Dark Knight', year: 2008 },
  { title: '12 Angry Men', year: 1957 },
];

movies.sort((a, b) => b.year - a.year);
```

This code sorts the `movies` array in descending order based on the `year` property of each object. The only difference from the previous example is that we're subtracting the `year` of `b` from the `year` of `a` instead of the other way around.

By doing so, we get the result sorted in descending order, that is, with the most recent year first.

Yes, certainly! Here's an example of how to sort an array of objects in ascending order based on a string property value:

```javascript
const fruits = [
  { name: 'apple', color: 'red' },
  { name: 'banana', color: 'yellow' },
  { name: 'mango', color: 'orange' },
  { name: 'kiwi', color: 'green' },
];

fruits.sort((a, b) => a.color.localeCompare(b.color));
```

In this example, we have an array of fruit objects sorted by their `color` property in alphabetical ascending order. 

The `sort` method takes a compare function that compares the `color` property of each object using the `localeCompare` method. This method compares two strings `a` and `b` by converting them to Unicode string forms, and then comparing the Unicode code points of each character in the strings. 

As a result, the `sort` method returns a sorted `fruits` array in ascending order by `color`.
